profile.campus: Stream Chicago, IL submarket (Elk Grove Village, ORDA site, separate campus from Chicago II)
profile.address: 2080 Lunt Avenue, Elk Grove Village, IL 60007
profile.reading: Stream Chicago I sits at 2080 Lunt Avenue in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, internally coded ORDA by the operator. Per Stream own site, the facility was acquired in December 2017 and subsequently reconstructed, providing 31 megawatts of capacity across 155,189 square feet, with a 2024 expansion adding a further 28,500 square feet on 1.10 acres. The facility was reported fully leased by the end of 2020 to an unnamed major cloud customer. Chicago I sits in the same Elk Grove Village submarket as Stream separate Chicago II facility on Busse Road, though Stream own site treats the two as sequential, separately developed campuses rather than one shared site, distinguished by different street addresses and different commissioning timelines. A third facility, referred to as Chicago III or ORDC, broke ground in September 2025 nearby on Landmeier Road, planned as more than 1.2 million square feet across three buildings with a dedicated ComEd substation and targeted service in 2027, underscoring the submarket continued growth. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds completed acquisition of a majority stake in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. Elk Grove Village sits in the O Hare International Airport industrial corridor northwest of downtown Chicago, an area that has become one of the Midwest most significant data center clusters given its fiber connectivity, airport proximity, and interstate access, factors consistent with Stream original 2017 decision to acquire and reconstruct a building in that specific submarket rather than build new elsewhere.
profile.research_note: 31 MW / 155,189 sqft (plus a 2024 +28,500 sqft expansion), Dec 2017 acquisition, fully leased by end 2020 sourced to Stream own Chicago I page. Explicitly noted as a separate campus from Chicago II per Stream own site, and the newer Chicago III/ORDC groundbreaking noted for submarket context without conflating it with this facility.
sources_tried: Streams own dedicated Chicago I page, Streams own Apollo acquisition press release, and Apollos own completion press release

reading.body:
Stream Chicago I holds 31 megawatts of IT capacity across 155,189 square feet in Elk Grove Village, Illinois. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, this implies roughly 775 racks. The facility was acquired and reconstructed by December 2017 and reported fully leased by the end of 2020 to an unnamed major cloud customer, meaning current utilization is not published.

Chicago I ranks seventh by published megawatts among the 44 mapped data center facilities in Illinois, representing 13 percent of the state's 236 published megawatts. Only six facilities in the state publish capacity figures, so this ranking reflects disclosure practice rather than a complete market picture. Stream operates Chicago I and the separate Chicago II facility in the same Elk Grove Village submarket as part of a broader regional cluster near O'Hare International Airport.

The capacity constraint at this stage is tenancy, not power delivery. Chicago I is reported fully leased since 2020, and its published specifications include no power availability for expansion. A third Stream facility, Chicago III, broke ground nearby in September 2025 as a 1.2-million-square-foot campus with a dedicated ComEd substation and planned service in 2027, indicating the operator's confidence in regional grid capacity and submarket demand.
